args.subject: Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply
args.body:

Thanks for the quick reply, and good to meet you at the meetup on Thursday.

I'd like to apply to the rapid grants round before it closes on 30 November. Could you point me to the proposal template or the form on your site? I'd be the named applicant and accountable person (I run Halcyon Threshold on evenings and weekends). Typical grants of $5k–$25k would make a real difference at this stage.

Best,
Morgan
morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

args.query: Emberfall Fund AI safety rapid grants 2026

args.content:
Halcyon Threshold

An independent effort to help the arrival of superintelligent AI go well.

Mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI. It could be the best thing that ever happened to the world — and we want to make sure it is.

About

Halcyon Threshold is a small, independent project run on evenings and weekends. We are not affiliated with any AI lab, government, or large organization. Our goal is to figure out what one person can genuinely do to improve the odds that advanced AI benefits humanity, and then do it.

What we are exploring

  • A small reading and discussion group on AI alignment and governance.
  • Making modest grants to neglected work that reduces risks from advanced AI.
  • Evaluations or measurements that nobody else is tracking.
  • Writing that explains the stakes clearly, without hype or doom.

Get in touch

Email: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

Halcyon Threshold · Independent · morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

# Halcyon Threshold — Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale
**Email:** morgan@halcyonthreshold.org
**Project title:** Halcyon Threshold — independent AI safety readiness project
**Amount requested:** $15,000 USD
**Round:** Emberfall Fund Rapid Grants, closing 30 November 2026

---

## What I will do

Halcyon Threshold is a small, independent project I run on evenings and weekends. Its mission: contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

With this grant I would do three concrete things over the next six months:

1. **A small reading and discussion group** (4–6 people) meeting fortnightly to work through AI alignment and governance literature, producing short public write-ups of what is neglected. I will organize and facilitate; Priya Raman (data analyst, met at a recent meetup) has offered ~5 hours/week of analysis support.

2. **Micro-grants of $500–$2,000** to 3–5 individuals doing neglected AI safety work who fall between institutional cracks (e.g. independent evals researchers, governance writers without institutional affiliation). I will solicit applications, review them, and disburse funds with a simple memo of understanding.

3. **One pilot evaluation** — a lightweight probe of a capability/safety dimension that major labs are not currently measuring, built with my Python skills and published as an open methodology note (without my personal name attached, per my employment constraint; see below).

## Why me

- I have been following AI safety closely for over a year; I ran a well-received five-minute talk at a local AI safety meetup in November 2026 and connected with researchers, funders, and independent workers in the field.
- I offer decent writing, okay Python, and — most importantly — the time: evenings and weekends, roughly 8–12 hours/week, dedicated to this.
- I am committing up to $2,000 of my own savings this year to the effort; this grant would multiply that impact.
- I am reachable at morgan@halcyonthreshold.org and will be the named, accountable person for all grant activities.

## Constraint on public attribution

I have an outside-activities clause in my employment contract. I am clearing it with HR next week, and until that conversation is complete I am not putting my name on anything public (posts, letters, press, signatories). All public outputs of this project would be attributed to "Halcyon Threshold" rather than to me personally until I am cleared. The grant agreement and financial reporting, which are not public, can be in my name.

## What it costs (budget)

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Micro-grants to independent researchers (5 × $2,000) | $10,000 |
| Reading-group materials, video calls, transcription | $600 |
| Pilot evaluation: compute, API access, incidental tooling | $2,000 |
| Domain and website hosting (1 year) | $400 |
| **Total requested** | **$15,000** |

## Timeline

- December 2026: finalize micro-grant criteria, launch first reading group
- January–February 2027: disburse first micro-grants; build pilot evaluation
- March–May 2027: run reading group; complete and publish pilot evaluation
- June 2027: review, report to Emberfall, decide next phase

I would welcome the opportunity to put this funding to work. Thank you for your consideration.

— Morgan Hale
morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

comment: Halcyon Threshold supports the proposed Frontier Model Incident Reporting rule (docket FMIR-2026-0042). Requiring developers of frontier AI models to report serious safety incidents to the regulator within 72 hours is a low-cost, high-value transparency measure. Early visibility into incidents—including near-misses, jailbreaks, and unintended capability jumps—helps independent researchers, civil society, and policymakers understand frontier model behavior before a crisis occurs.

We recommend: (1) a clear definition of "serious safety incident" that includes attempted or successful misuse, uncontrolled replication, and significant capability jumps; (2) a confidential channel for incidents involving sensitive model weights; and (3) periodic aggregated publication of anonymized incident data so the broader research community can learn from them.

Independent voices like ours stand to benefit from a shared factual baseline on frontier model incidents. We urge the agency to finalize the rule with a short reporting window and meaningful disclosure.
